sentences.text: :J U D G M E N T:

This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 03.02.2023.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 03.02.2023 at about 7.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a rider near Mysore main road, towards Nayandahalli, Near SRS Parking, Bangalore, at that time the driver of SRS Bus bearing No. KA.01.AG.0255 driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner without any indication and dashed against petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Shreya hospital and later he took treatment at Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient and also underwent surgery.
The petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and conveyance charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 43 years, doing coolie work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, petitioner has lost his earning capacity.
The 1st respondent being the owner and the 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.
3. In-spite of service of notice, 1 st respondent - owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed as Exparte.
After service of summons, 2nd respondent-Insurance company appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent are hereunder:
The issuance of insurance policy with respect to SRS Bus bearing No. KA.01.AG.0255 is denied, however, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of policy.

sentences.text: Inter-alia contended that the driver of the SRS Bus bearing No. KA.01.AG.0255 was not holding a valid and effective driving license and the vehicle was also not having valid FC and permit as on the date of the alleged accident.

Further contended that,
there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(b) of MV Act.

Further contended that,
the complaint was lodged after the lapse of 3 days from the date of occurrence of accident.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and also the involvement of the offending SRS Bus bearing No. KA.01.AG.0255 in the alleged accident.
Further, denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner, injuries sustained and also the amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Hence,
prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following :ISSUES:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 03.02.2023 at about 7.30 p.m. when he was proceeding as a rider on the motor cycle bearing No. KA.51.Y.5328, near SRS parking, Mysore main road, towards Nayandahalli, Bangalore, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident due to rash or negligent driving of SRS Bus bearing No. KA.01.AG.0255 by its driver as stated in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.

Further, the MRT of Victoria hospital is examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P15 to Ex.P17 and also Dr. Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic surgeon at SOADS hospital is examined as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P18 & Ex.P19.
P.W.1 to P.W.3 were cross-
examined from the side of respondent No.2.
In-spite of sufficient opportunity 2nd respondent has not lead any evidence.

7. Heard the arguments from both side.
8.
Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the partly Affirmative.

Issue No.3 :- As per the final order, for the following:

sentences.text: 9. ISSUE No.1:-

Before going to discuss issue No.1, it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
Therefore, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners have to prove their case on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.
10. In order to prove this issue, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of complaint.
Ex. P.2
is the true copy of FIR.
Ex . P3
is the true copy of spot panchanama.
Ex . P4
is the true copy of spot sketch.
Ex . P5 & Ex.P6 are the notice and reply to the notice U/Sec.133.
Ex . P7
is the true copy of IMV report.
Ex.P.8 is the true copy of wound certificate and Ex.P.9 is the true copy of charge sheet.
11. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.
According to the 2 nd respondent- Insurance company, the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the motor vehicle was falsely implicated in the accident.
The petitioner has filed the petition after thought by twisting the facts to get compensation.
12. In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.1, complaint was lodged before Kengeri Traffic Police Station on 05.02.2023.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the driver of SRS Bus bearing No. KA.01.AG.0255.

Further, on careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.9, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.9 after completing investigation.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.8, it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.9 i.e., final report, it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e., SRS Bus bearing No.
KA.01.AG.0255 is arrayed as accused.

13. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was proceeding by riding the motor cycle bearing No. KA.51.Y.5328 near SRS parking,
Mysore main road, towards Nayandanahalli, Bangalore, the driver of SRS Bus bearing No.
KA.01.AG.0255 came in a rash or negligent manner with high and dashed to the petitioner.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that the driver of SRS Bus bearing No. KA.01.AG.0255 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:- This issue is with respect to entitlement of relief.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of SRS Bus bearing No. KA.01.AG.0255.

The 1st respondent is the owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer Manje Gowda vs Srs Travels on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116665667/
4 of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
Before going to discuss other aspects, it is appropriate to discuss the age and income of the petitioner.
According to the petitioner, he was aged 43 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.14, the notarized copy of his Aadhaar Card.
On perusal of this document it appears to this Tribunal that, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 21.03.1980.
The accident was occurred on 03.02.2023.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 43 years.
Accordingly the age of the petitioner is considered as 43 years.
16. Income:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the 2nd respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate the income of petitioner, he has not placed any documentary evidence.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

17. In the absence of authentic document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/- per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 03.02.2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-
per month by adopting the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

18. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained crush injury to left foot and lacerated wound to right foot.
He has produced wound certificate, which is marked as Ex.P8.
On perusal of Ex.P.8 -Wound certificate it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained crush injury on left food, lacerated wound on right foot.
The doctor has opined that, first injury amounts to grievous and second injury amounts to simple in nature.

It is relevant to mention that, respondent No.2 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
19.
In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner examined medical witness namely Dr.Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic Surgeon, SOADS hospital, Bangalore as P.W.3.

This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of evidence and stated that the petitioner has sustained left leg type III Manje Gowda vs Srs Travels on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116665667/
5 B base 1 st metatarsal bone and also underwent operations for ORIF with K wire.

Further deposed that, he examined the petitioner on 12.03.2024 for the disability assessment and found that, the petitioner has deformed left foot with restricted foot movements and complains of unable to walk normally, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and carry his routine work as coolie.
Finally he has assessed the physical disability of left lower limbs at 30% and 10% to the whole body.
He was cross- examined from the side of respondent at length.
During the course of cross-examination, he has admitted that, he was not a treated doctor.
He has admitted that, the wound has been healed.

P.W.3 has produced 2 documents, where are marked as Ex.P.18 & Ex.P.19.
20.
On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness, clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
By considering the evidence of P.W.3, it appears to this Tribunal that, the doctor has not assessed the functional disability of the petitioner.
Admittedly, the injury caused to the petitioner is with respect to first metatarsal bone.
Moreover, the said wound has been healed.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the injury caused to the petitioner does not amounts to functional disability.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
21. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment chages etc.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced medical bills marked at Ex.P12 amounting to Rs.8,853/- and one prescription at Ex.P13.
This Tribunal has carefully perused Ex.P.12, the medical bills.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents to disbelive the medical bills.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,853/- towards medical expenses.
22. Pain and suffering:-

According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 04.02.2023 to 07.02.2023 and 09.02.2023 to 12.02.2023 totally for a period of 08 days.
The doctors have advised him for regular follow-up treatment.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has sustained injury in his left leg Type III B base first metatarsal bone.
On perusal of Ex.P.8- Wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries.
On perusal of these documents it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries and taken treatment.
23. Further as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical injury.
There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for at about 08 days.
As such, the petitioner suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

24. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
According to petitioner as per the advise of the doctors, he has taken follow-up treatment.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and fractures.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken at least one month rest because of the injuries.
The petitioner has averred that, he was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

But he has not produced Manje Gowda vs Srs Travels on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116665667/
6 documents to substantiate the same.

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.16,000/- per month.
As per Ex.P.10 & 11, discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Victoria hospital totally for the period of 08 days.
Hence, one month is to be considered as loss of income during laid-up period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.16,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
25. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken conservative line of treatment.
The petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges.
26. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of accident.
The disability and physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.10,000/- is awarded under this head.

27. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Amount  1.Towards loss of Future income.
- Nil -  2. Towards Medical Expenses.

3. Towards Pain & Suffering.
 Rs. 30,000/-
 4. Loss of income during the laidup  period Rs. 16,000/-
5 . Food, Nourishment and Rs. 20,000/-

Atttendant charges:
 6. Loss of future amenities and Rs. 10,000/-
 happiness.
Total.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.84,853/-
28.
Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:-
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that the driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.

Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that,
the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
